content.comment_body: I am using a [product_name] from the [version_no] series with the standard display module. I want to be able to adjust several values directly from the display, and I thought combining two function keys with the arrow keys would help prevent accidental changes. In simulation, everything works as intended, but on the physical device, it doesn't function at all. Does anyone know why this might be happening? Are there alternative ways to safely modify 6-8 values from the display?

Hello, Could you clarify what exactly isn't working? Did you know you need to use the ESC key alongside the arrow keys? Is it possible to press F1 and F2 to activate a message, while pressing ESC and a cursor key at the same time? In simulation, this setup works, but in practice it's difficult. You might want to check the example applications for menu structures. Using password protection can help prevent unwanted modifications. Regards,

analysis.insight_summary: A user is trying to set up a [product_name] with a display module to allow editing of several values via a combination of function and arrow keys. This approach works in simulation but not on the actual hardware, resulting in confusion about key sequences and differing behaviors between simulated and real environments. Suggestions included consulting documentation and implementing additional input security measures.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the logic designed in simulation to function exactly the same on actual hardware, seeking a consistent and secure method to change several parameters from the display without risk of unintended changes.
